bible_refs.note: The Greek quotation matches Acts 2:1-4 in content: gathering, Pentecost, sound like wind, tongues of fire, speaking in other tongues.
The transformation of Carmel into a wilderness and then a forest echoes Isaiah 32:15, where the wilderness becomes a fruitful field and the fruitful field is counted as a forest.

choices.why: The verb καταχερσόω literally means to cover with dung or filth, used metaphorically for divine judgment or defilement due to wickedness (ἐξήνιον).

In this context, δρυμός refers to a wooded area, specifically contrasted with cultivated land; the author defines it as wild wood useful for burning, not a literal forest of trees but a wild, unusable thicket.
The phrase ἀγρίαν ὕλην is explicitly defined by the author as wood whose use is for burning, indicating uncultivated, combustible brush rather than timber forest.

Then he adds saying: 'Why have you broken down its fence, so that all who pass by the way pluck it? A boar from the forest has ravaged it, and a wild beast has fed upon it.' For in this manner the possessions of fields, scattered abroad, the owners cast away, and to them no word, even if any harm were brought upon them; so also our benevolent God lets go the soul, and shows complete lack of pity, naked, if a fruitless desert should happen for good works; until there comes upon you the Spirit from on high. And it shall be that Carmel becomes a desert, and Carmel shall be reckoned as a forest. And justice shall dwell in the desert, and righteousness shall settle in Carmel. And the works of righteousness shall be peace, and righteousness shall possess rest, and those who trust shall be at rest forever. And his people shall dwell in a city of peace, and shall inhabit being confident, and shall rest with wealth. He makes evident also the time, in which the intellectually fruitful shall be a desert, the offspring of Israel who have been disobedient. For he transfers the word upon the earth, I say, to those who have valued obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ, and having been purified indeed through faith in him, and having become partakers of the Holy Spirit.

pass_b_english: For it will be, he says, the promised things, and Israel will be smeared with dung because of its wickedness, until the Spirit from on high comes upon you (Isaiah 32:15).
As we have read in the Acts of the Holy Apostles: they were all together in one place, about the days of the holy Pentecost (Acts 2:1).
And behold, suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a mighty wind blowing, and it filled the house where they were gathered (Acts 2:2).
And there appeared to them tongues as of fire, distributed, and they sat upon each one of them, and they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance (Acts 2:3-4).
Therefore when, he says, the Spirit from above and from on high, the Spirit of God, comes upon you who believe, then also the Carmel will be a wilderness (Isaiah 32:15).
The Carmel is either Mount Carmel, a very great mountain in Judea, and wood of date palms, row upon row.
Thus he likens both Jerusalem herself and all the region around dwellings to Carmel, which also has an innumerable multitude of inhabitants.
But it will be, he says, a wilderness and will be counted as a forest (Isaiah 32:15).
By forest he means the wild wood, whose need is for burning, for they cut down the unseasoned woods, and flame…
